mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, it signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates, reducing the present value of future equity cash flows and thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% from the prior month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rise is not followed by a discount-rate increase in macro models.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 6% for two consecutive months predicts a labor-market softening, which reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 6% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In the 20-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are positive or at least not statistically different from the prior month (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO rises above 95.0 (monthly), it indicates strengthening manufacturing capacity, which supports higher long-run earnings growth and pushes S&P 500 60-day forward returns positive.
failure_condition: Over 12 months after INDPRO crosses above 95.0, SPX 60-day forward returns show no outperformance versus a pre-expansion baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in HOUST and PAYEMS above their 50th percentile for three consecutive months indicate a dual labor and inventory demand surge, which elevates earnings expectations and drives S&P 500 20-day forward returns positive.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 50th percentile AND PAYEMS > 50th percentile for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In the 20-day window after the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are negative or flat, and earnings surprise forecasts do not rise above historical averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS below 120,000 in a month followed by a rebound above 125,000 signals a labor-market correction that precedes a recovery, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns positive as market anticipates stabilization.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 120,000 AND PAYEMS > 125,000 in the following month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain negative in the month following the rebound, or the rebound in PAYEMS is not followed by a positive return signal.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 221.0 (monthly), it reflects accelerating price pressures that the Fed is likely to respond to with rate hikes, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the subsequent 60 days, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-inflation spike baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 of at least 3% for two consecutive quarters is interpreted as a deepening demand shortfall, which depresses corporate profits and yields negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by ≥3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In the 20-day window after the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or GDPC1 decline is not followed by a profit-downgrade consensus.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in UNRATE and HOUST below their 30th percentile for two months indicates a dual softening in wage growth and job creation, which increases risk premia and pushes S&P 500 20-day forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 30th percentile AND HOUST < 30th percentile for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not negative or are positive in at least 60% of similar trigger windows (walk-forward split test).
